name: Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD)
description: MACD measures the relationship between two EMAs to identify trend direction, momentum, and potential reversals. It consists of the MACD line (12 EMA minus 26 EMA), a signal line (9 EMA of MACD), and a histogram (MACD minus signal). It functions as both a trend-following and momentum indicator. Most effective in trending markets; generates false signals in choppy, ranging conditions.

signals.condition: MACD line crosses above zero line
signals.interpretation: Bullish trend signal: 12 EMA has crossed above 26 EMA; indicates the broader trend has shifted bullish — use as trend bias confirmation, not entry

signals.condition: MACD line crosses below zero line
signals.interpretation: Bearish trend signal: 12 EMA has crossed below 26 EMA; indicates the broader trend has shifted bearish — use as trend bias confirmation, not entry

signals.condition: MACD line crosses above signal line
signals.interpretation: Bullish entry timing signal; momentum is shifting upward; more reliable when the cross occurs below the zero line (oversold territory)

signals.condition: MACD line crosses below signal line
signals.interpretation: Bearish entry timing signal; momentum is shifting downward; more reliable when the cross occurs above the zero line (overbought territory)

signals.condition: MACD line above zero and above signal line
signals.interpretation: Bullish momentum; trend is up and accelerating; favor long bias

signals.condition: MACD line below zero and below signal line
signals.interpretation: Bearish momentum; trend is down and accelerating; favor short bias

signals.condition: Histogram making lower highs while price makes higher highs (bearish histogram divergence)
signals.interpretation: Leading warning of weakening bullish momentum; potential trend reversal or significant pullback approaching

signals.condition: Histogram making higher lows while price makes lower lows (bullish histogram divergence)
signals.interpretation: Leading warning of weakening bearish momentum; potential trend reversal or significant bounce approaching

signals.condition: MACD line diverges from price: price higher high, MACD lower high
signals.interpretation: Classic bearish divergence; momentum is not confirming price move; reversal risk elevated

signals.condition: MACD line diverges from price: price lower low, MACD higher low
signals.interpretation: Classic bullish divergence; selling momentum is exhausting; reversal risk elevated

signals.condition: Histogram bars are shrinking after a sustained move
signals.interpretation: Momentum is decelerating; trend may be losing steam; watch for signal line cross

signals.condition: Histogram bars expanding in trend direction
signals.interpretation: Momentum is accelerating; trend is strong; avoid fading the move

rules.rule: Use zero-line crosses for trend direction bias only, not as entry triggers. Wait for a pullback and a signal-line cross in the trend direction after a zero-line cross.
rules.rationale: Zero-line crosses lag significantly. Entering at the cross typically results in poor risk-to-reward as the initial move is often already extended.

rules.rule: Use signal-line crosses for entry timing, not as standalone entries. The cross must align with the trend direction established by the zero-line and price structure.
rules.rationale: Counter-trend signal-line crosses in ranging markets generate excessive whipsaws. Trend alignment filters out the majority of false signals.

rules.rule: Treat histogram divergence as a leading warning, not an immediate entry. Divergence can persist for multiple bars. Wait for the signal-line cross or price structure break to confirm.
rules.rationale: Histogram divergence identifies momentum shifts early but price can continue in the original direction for some time before reversing.

rules.rule: Avoid MACD signals in clearly ranging, sideways markets. MACD generates excessive false crossovers when price is oscillating without directional trend.
rules.rationale: MACD is derived from EMAs, which are trend-following by nature. In ranges, the EMAs converge and diverge repeatedly without directional conviction.

rules.rule: The most reliable signal-line crosses are those that occur after a deep pullback toward or below the zero line in an uptrend, or after a bounce toward or above the zero line in a downtrend.
rules.rationale: These crosses represent momentum resuming from a corrective move, aligning with the higher-timeframe trend for maximum probability.

rules.rule: Monitor the MACD on the higher timeframe to establish trend bias, then drop to the lower timeframe for signal-line cross entries.
rules.rationale: Multi-timeframe MACD alignment (higher TF zero-line position + lower TF signal cross) produces significantly more reliable entries.

rules.rule: Do not rely on MACD alone for volatile, news-driven instruments. Sudden price spikes can distort MACD readings and produce meaningless crosses.
rules.rationale: EMA-based indicators are sensitive to sharp price spikes that create artificial divergences and crosses not representative of sustainable momentum.

agent_use: Use MACD to determine trend bias and momentum phase. First check zero-line position: above zero = bullish bias, below zero = bearish bias. Then check MACD vs signal line position to confirm momentum direction. Monitor histogram for divergence as early reversal warning. Use signal-line crosses only in the direction of zero-line bias and price structure. Flag histogram divergence as a caution tag on any active trend signal. In ranging conditions, suppress MACD-based entry signals and note 'MACD unreliable in current range'. Report MACD line value, signal line value, histogram direction, zero-line bias, and any active divergence in analysis output.
